page: Microsoft Azure E16bds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Ebdsv6 series, powered by Intel x86_64 processors managed through the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs paired with 128 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It features no GPU accelerators and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

A key architectural aspect of the E16bds_v6 is its local storage configuration, incorporating 944 GB of direct-attached NVMe solid-state storage. In addition to local disk performance, the instance profile supports high remote block storage throughput and is compatible with Azure Premium Storage options. This dual-storage capability allows workloads to partition volatile, high-IOPS operations on local NVMe while maintaining persistent data across enterprise block volumes.

From an operational and resource standpoint, the instance balances dense memory provisioning with dedicated compute and high storage throughput. The high RAM allocation relative to core count reduces the per-gigabyte overhead for data-intensive engines that do not require excessive compute threads. Tradeoffs include the lack of bundled public IPv4 routing and the ephemeral nature of local NVMe storage, requiring architectures that account for external persistence or replication.

The E16bds_v6 is configured for workloads requiring large active datasets and fast disk caching, such as relational databases, in-memory caching solutions, large transactional systems, data analytics pipelines, and enterprise enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems.
